rationale:
bugs_open/390, commit 3 of 3 - the agent stops guessing. Commits 1 and 2 are both council-APPROVED and both LIVE: migration 616 (corr ef5f9a0d, approved round 2) corrected the prompt that instructed the losing move, and the cascade attribution (corr 058b59b6, approved round 1) rolled to all three services at ~23:11 on 2026-08-25 (stamp 2fb40a96; commit ea64845e0 confirmed an ancestor, chassis confirmed by binary probe with an absent-sha control).

WHAT THE ATTRIBUTION NOW WRITES, that nothing yet reads. Every new contrast_failure filed by a cascade/v1 adapter carries `spec.repair_surface` (theme / unreachable / unattributed), `spec.winning_rule` (the declaration PROVEN to decide the colour - proven by removing it in the page and watching the computed value move), and `spec.override_requirement` (minimum specificity computed with cascadia, strictness, !important parity, plus an `override_example` the platform verified with satisfiesRequirement). css-patch-agent still authors under 616's blanket !important guidance and still spends an LLM call on findings no stylesheet can repair.

THIS MIGRATION, two changes on the one live css-patch-agent row:

(1) A `check_repair_surface` conditional_branch between check_base_integrity and plan_css_fix. `repair_surface == 'unreachable'` - the winner is an !important declaration in the element's own style attribute, which no stylesheet rule can outrank at ANY specificity - parks at needs_human_review with `parked_by='css_cascade_unreachable_390'` BEFORE any LLM spend, in exactly 542/546's stamp-then-terminal shape (next_step complete_refused, the existing terminal). Authoring a rule for that finding is the bug itself: it completes and does nothing.

(2) The prompt renders the measured requirement when present, inside {{if .input_data.spec.override_requirement}}: the winning declaration, the specificity bar, whether a tie suffices or strictness is needed, and !important ONLY where importance parity demands it - superseding 616's blanket instruction on exactly the rows where the platform now knows better. Rows without the fields keep 616's guidance byte-for-byte.

SKEW SAFETY, verified not asserted, in every order:
- a legacy/unattributed row has no repair_surface; conditional_branch's compareValues(nil, expected) returns false unless expected is null/nil/empty (conditional_branch_action.go:518-521, re-read 2026-08-26), so the gate routes to plan_css_fix - today's path;
- the template block is fenced on override_requirement, NOT winning_rule, deliberately: the filer writes winning_rule for a VERIFIED unreachable winner too (where req is nil), and a template dereferencing a missing sibling map errors at execute time and would fail the whole LLM step. The EXACT post-apply prompt - extracted from the database after running the apply block in a rolled-back transaction, not a hand-copy - was parsed and executed with Go text/template against a full spec and a legacy spec: parses clean, full render carries the requirement, legacy render is byte-equivalent in behaviour to 616's (block vanishes, no error).

WHY THE PARK CANNOT STRAND A FINDING: needs_human_review is in NEITHER workItemTerminalStatuses (the row keeps its dedup slot, so the finding cannot re-file while parked) NOR workItemClosedStatuses (so WII-016's retraction still closes it when a page rebuild removes the inline offender and the next audit stops observing the pairing). Self-draining on positive evidence, like the css_no_theme_198 parks.

GUARDS, in the hardened one-DO-block style 616's round 2 settled (every literal declared once; row-count assertion before any read or write; GET DIAGNOSTICS after the UPDATE). Mutation-proven in rolled-back transactions against the live row: a second active row raises; 616's text removed underneath raises; check_base_integrity rewired by another lane raises. Round trip proven: apply then ROLLBACK file, one transaction, restores 616's shape exactly.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: nothing for `unattributed` (routes to the LLM as today - parking on "we do not know" would park the whole legacy backlog); nothing about completion semantics (owner: routing first); nothing about erasure (bugs_open/396).

plan.summary: One migration on the live css-patch-agent row: a check_repair_surface gate that parks browser-proven-unreachable findings before any LLM spend (542's stamp-then-terminal shape, self-draining via WII-016), and a prompt block that renders the measured override requirement where present, superseding 616's blanket !important on exactly the rows where the platform now knows better.

plan.risks:
1) EXPECTED OBJECTION - 'the gate has never seen a live unreachable row.' True: zero cascade-attributed rows exist (no audit has run since the roll). The then-arm is therefore unexercised in production at apply time. Three things bound this: the arm is config, not code, and its exact condition literal is pinned by VERIFY; the else-arm IS today's live path, proven by the legacy-shape template execution and the nil-comparison source; and the first attributed rows will exercise it within the 3-day rotation window, with the parked_by marker making the census one query. Pre-registered prediction P4 in the lane NOTES states the expected distribution and its disconfirming result.

2) The park lands in the needs_human_review queue that bugs_open/033 says has no working surface. Same posture as the css_no_theme_198 parks it sits beside: self-draining via WII-016 retraction on positive re-measurement, and the expected population is SMALL (an !important inline style attribute was 0 of 40 in the sampled population; the sample was of completions, so a standing population may differ - the marker census is the check).

3) A prompt-template execute error would fail every css_fix step. Bounded by proving the EXACT post-apply artefact parses and executes on five data shapes, including the two absence shapes; and the fence choice (override_requirement, not winning_rule) exists specifically because the sibling-absent case is an execute-time error in text/template.

4) Concurrent lanes: 617-634 were taken by other lanes in one overnight window and the row's updated_at moved once already; the drift guards abort loudly on every anchor this migration depends on, and each was mutation-proven to fire.

5) 616's blanket !important remains the fallback for unattributed/legacy rows by design. The measured block only supersedes it where the platform has proof. If the council prefers the blanket retired entirely once attribution coverage is high, that is a later migration with a coverage measurement in front of it - not this one.
